title: Fix duplicate batches on CSV import retry

rows.title: A batch hit twice by a transient lock is retried and stored once
rows.observed: Import printed 'import 1: 5 rows in 3 batches', exit=0, stderr had retry 1/3 and retry 2/3. list: '1 samples/products.csv done batches=3 rows=5 stored=5'.

rows.title: The reported case: one transient lock after the rows are written, then a retry
rows.observed: Import printed 'import 1: 5 rows in 3 batches', exit=0, one 'retry 1/3' line. list: done batches=3 rows=5 stored=5 (the report says it was 7 before the fix; not re-checked here).

rows.title: The lock outlasts the retries: the import fails visibly and leaves no doubled or half batch
rows.observed: exit=1; stderr 'retry 1/1' then 'error: storage failed after retries: database is locked'. list: '1 samples/products.csv failed batches=0 rows=0 stored=0'.

rows.title: A messy CSV (BOM, CRLF, padded cells, quoted comma, accented name) under two transient locks stores each row once
rows.observed: Import printed 'import 1: 5 rows in 3 batches', exit=0, retry 1/3 and 2/3. list: done batches=3 rows=5 stored=5.

rows.title: A messy TSV, one row per batch, with locks both before and after the rows are written
rows.observed: Import printed 'import 1: 3 rows in 3 batches', exit=0, retries 1/3, 2/3, 3/3. list: done batches=3 rows=3 stored=3.

rows.title: A plain CSV import with no faults works as before
rows.observed: Import printed exactly 'import 1: 5 rows in 3 batches', exit=0, no stderr. list: done batches=3 rows=5 stored=5.

rows.title: A dry run counts the rows and writes nothing
rows.observed: Printed 'dry run: 3 rows in 1 batches, nothing written', exit=0. ls of the evidence folder showed it empty: no s7.db.

rows.title: Every CLI flag is still accepted
rows.observed: import --help lists file, --db DB, --retries RETRIES, --batch-size BATCH_SIZE, --dry-run; list --help lists --db DB. import with --retries 0 --batch-size 1: 'import 1: 3 rows in 3 batches' exit=0; with --dry-run: 'dry run: 3 rows in 2 batches, nothing written' exit=0; list: stored=3 exit=0.

rows.title: A bad row stops the import with a clear message and keeps the earlier batch once
rows.observed: exit=2; stderr "error: line 4: bad row {'sku': 'E-502', 'name': 'Broken', 'qty': 'lots'}". list: '1 ... failed batches=1 rows=2 stored=2'.
